target.title: feat(web): restore the last project location

scenario.expected: The exact project, pathname, query, and fragment are stored.
scenario.observed: GET /api/v1/workspace/ui-state returned projectId cezar, pathname /p/cezar/git, search ?qa=fresh-7aec, and hash #changed.

scenario.action: Open the exact bare root and then use browser Back.
scenario.expected: The bare root is replaced by the saved route without leaving a transient root entry in history.
scenario.observed: The URL restored to /p/cezar/git?qa=fresh-7aec#changed; Back remained on that restored URL.

scenario.action: Open an explicit project Settings URL, visit global Settings, switch to a 390x844 viewport, and open the bare root.
scenario.expected: The explicit project URL remains authoritative, global Settings does not overwrite it, and the mobile restoration is usable.
scenario.observed: Workspace UI state remained /p/cezar/settings/agents?manual=fresh-7aec#config after visiting global Settings; the bare root restored that exact URL and the Agents pane rendered without page or console errors.

scenario.action: Seed a structurally valid saved route for a removed project and open the bare root.
scenario.expected: The stale location is ignored and the boot project Tasks page is used.
scenario.observed: The URL became /p/42766454-3ead-4ea4-8f05-aab273e5cf8b/ and the responsive Tasks empty state rendered without page or console errors.

notes: The production build ran under CEZ_DRY_RUN=1 with an isolated CEZ_HOME, so no real agent credentials or developer workspace state were exercised.
The host /tmp quota was exhausted. The browser provider succeeded after its disposable Chrome profile was placed in /dev/shm; this was an environment workaround, not a product change.
This evidence-only run did not add qa-approved.
